INDEPENDENT REFERENCE for this epic, built before it starts. Base R, no package code. n=48, p=12, R=4 runs, 500 replications, NULL data throughout, crossnobis over all ordered evaluation edges, Sigma estimated either from training runs only (excluding both evaluated runs) or from all runs including the evaluated ones.

  shrinkage 0     train-only z +0.88   all-runs z +1.08   paired difference +0.000045 se 0.000158 z +0.29
  shrinkage 0.05  train-only z +0.63   all-runs z +0.96   paired difference +0.000118 se 0.000141 z +0.83
  shrinkage 0.2   train-only z +0.11   all-runs z +0.16   paired difference +0.000019 se 0.000096 z +0.19

NO DETECTABLE LEAKAGE at any shrinkage level. Both policies keep the null centred, and the paired difference - the sensitive comparison, since it removes shared noise - never exceeds 0.83 standard errors.

That is the theoretically expected answer. In a Gaussian linear model the residuals are exactly orthogonal to the fitted coefficients, so Sigma_hat built from a run residuals is independent of that run beta_hat. Reusing evaluation-run residuals does not contaminate the crossnobis estimate, and shrinkage toward a diagonal computed from the same residuals does not break it at these levels.

THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT, which changes how this epic should be designed

This is an EQUIVALENCE study, not a difference study. "No significant difference at N replications" is a statement about power, not about leakage. If Epic 7 concludes the two provenance policies are interchangeable, it needs an equivalence margin and the power to back it, not a failed significance test.

Concretely: state the margin first - for example "the two policies agree to within 0.005 on the null in these units" - then choose replications so the paired standard error supports it. At 500 replications the paired se here is ~1e-4, so this configuration can certify equivalence to roughly 3e-4. Reported that way the claim is defensible; reported as p > 0.05 it is not.

SCOPE CONDITION worth stating in the result

My simulation satisfies the Gaussian linear model exactly, which is precisely the condition that makes orthogonality hold. The realistic leakage risks live outside it: misspecified design, temporal autocorrelation estimated from the same data, or a data-dependent shrinkage target with more structure than a diagonal. The honest conclusion is conditional - the policies are equivalent WHEN the model is correctly specified - and the epic is worth more if it runs one misspecified arm alongside the well-specified one.
